</style><style data-tailwind-stylesheet="true"></style><p>Optimizely Content Management System (CMS) (SaaS) provides web content management through a UI that lets users work efficiently with content.</p>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note"></a></h3><p>Before editors can create content in CMS (SaaS), administrators and developers must implement a <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/content-modeling-saas">content model</a> that is modular and reusable to ensure consistency and reduce redundancy. A robust content model supports your project's immediate needs and its long-term evolution.</p><p>See <a target="_self" href="https://optimizely.navattic.com/cms-content-modeling">an interactive demo</a> on how to approach content modeling in Optimizely CMS (SaaS) and Visual Builder.</p></blockquote>
<p>Enter your username and password in the Optimizely login dialog box, and click <strong>Log In</strong>.</p>
<p>After logging in, your implementation and <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/access-rights">access rights</a> control the options you see.</p>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="general-features"></div><div class="heading-text">General features</div><a aria-label="Skip link to General features" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#general-features"></a></h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Context-sensitive actions</strong> – Some features are only available in certain contexts. The toolbar (for example) presents relevant actions depending on what you are currently doing, and the add (+) button also offers context-sensitive options.</li>
<li><strong>Primary actions</strong> – Some actions open in a window, such as a page delete confirmation. The background is then dimmed, meaning you must finish the primary action to continue.</li>
<li><strong>Action feedback and notifications</strong> – A message in the notification bar confirms successful actions. A notification may also display if an error requires you to take action.</li>
<li><strong>Drag-and-drop operations</strong> – Drag-and-drop is supported in many areas. For example, you can drag pages, media files, and shared blocks into the rich-text area or content areas or rearrange the page tree structure using drag-and-drop.</li>
<li><strong>Tooltips</strong> – Hover over a button or field, and a short tooltip displays.</li>
<li><strong>Keyboard commands</strong> – Standard keyboard commands are supported in many areas, such as moving pages in the page tree or the rich-text editor.</li>
<li><strong>Search</strong> – Supported in many areas to locate, such as pages in the page tree or media in the folder structure.</li>
<li><strong>Adaptable work environment</strong> – Resize and pin the panes depending on what you are currently doing, and add and remove gadgets of your choice for quick access to functionality.</li>
<li><strong>Support for time zones</strong> – Publishing actions in the edit view is done in your local time zone, whereas administrative actions are based on server time.</li>
<li><strong>Context menus</strong> – Available in many areas, such as the panes, page tree, and item listings. The menu displays different options depending on where you are in the interface and what you are doing.</li>
</ul>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="cms-saas-dashboard"></div><div class="heading-text">CMS (SaaS) dashboard</div><a aria-label="Skip link to CMS (SaaS) dashboard" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#cms-saas-dashboard"></a></h2>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-1"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-1"></a></h3><p>You must have at least edit privileges to see the CMS (SaaS) dashboard. See <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/access-rights">Access rights</a>.</p></blockquote>
<p>The CMS (SaaS) dashboard provides a centralized view of your content that lets you access and manage information from a single location. Each tab displays key information about your CMS (SaaS) instance.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/3abcf090e1ca4ea80dd8e4ffb7b9409794dde1c67f8ad6705559faae0521923b-dashboard-graphiql.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Define Content</strong> – Click <strong>Model Content</strong> to open the <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/settings">CMS (SaaS) settings</a>. You can also access the following links:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>REST API</strong> – Opens <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/introduction-to-the-cms-content-api">Introduction to the CMS (SaaS) REST API</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Manage API Keys</strong> – Opens <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>API Keys</strong>. See <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/api-keys">API Keys</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Developer Documentation</strong> – Opens the developer <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/get-started-saas">Get started</a> documentation.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Create Content</strong> – Click <strong>Create Content</strong> to open the Edit view. See <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/get-started-with-visual-builder">Get started with Visual Builder</a> and <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/all-properties-editing-view">All Properties editing view</a>. You can also access the following links:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>REST API</strong> – Opens <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/introduction-to-the-cms-content-api">Introduction to the CMS (SaaS) REST API</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Import Content</strong> – Opens <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>Import Content</strong>. See <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/import-data-into-cms-saas">Import data into CMS (SaaS)</a>.</li>
<li><strong>User documentation</strong> – Opens this document.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Render Content</strong> – Open Optimizely Graph to render content with the following links:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Graph Keys</strong> – Opens <strong>Settings</strong> > <strong>API Keys</strong>. See <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/api-keys">API Keys</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Configure Preview</strong>  – Opens <a target="_self" href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/enable-live-preview-saas">Enable Live Preview</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Examples</strong> – Opens <a target="_self" href="https://github.com/episerver/content-graph-js-sdk">Github with examples of Optimizely Graph</a>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Browse the graph</strong> – Opens <a target="_self" href="https://app-ocxcvbinterm6p85p001.cms.optimizely.com/ui/contentgraph/graphiql">Optimizely Graph</a>.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/064c60853b453a17c23f346275f22d31c3b9162fcf42706381e11b5c2f95feda-image_1.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>

<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-2"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-2"></a></h3><div class="readme-tailwind"><ul>
<li>Access the Standard GraphQL API through the URL <a target="_self" href="https://cg.optimizely.com/content/v2?auth=%7Bsinglekey%7D">https://cg.optimizely.com/content/v2?auth={singlekey}</a>. Use the single key you received when your account was created.</li>
<li>Access the Latest GraphQL API through the URL <a target="_self" href="https://latest.cg.optimizely.com//content/v2?auth=%7Bsinglekey%7D">https://latest.cg.optimizely.com//content/v2?auth={singlekey}</a>. Use the single key you received when your account was created.</li>
</ul></div></blockquote>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Workflow Status</strong> – Click any of the tabs, and click any link names to go directly to edit the page. You can sort the <strong>Name</strong>, <strong>Last modified</strong>, and <strong>Modified by</strong> columns by clicking the column headings. You can also select <strong>More</strong> (<strong>...</strong>) to edit the page or edit the workflow for that page. See <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/approval-sequences">Approval sequences</a>. </p>
<p>The following image shows workflow status activity on 29 pages: 23 <strong>Drafts</strong>, three <strong>In Review</strong>, and one each of <strong>Approved</strong>, <strong>Scheduled</strong>, or <strong>Rejected</strong> status. It also shows 22 broken links. When the dashboard is loaded, each tab displays numbers. To update the numbers, click the tab titles. It also shows the languages in which you can view the information.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/d6831410a81ba4ccc09f069b4cb5d13ffa761aceb50c11bfcdcc73832f6791ab-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Broken Links</strong> – Click a content link to fix any broken links, if applicable. This section shows the number of broken links in the database and lists the pages with at least one broken link. If there is more than one broken link on a page, the page is listed only once. For example, if you have only one page with 25 broken links, it displays 25 with a list of only one page. If you have 25 pages with one broken link each, it displays 25 broken links with a list of 25 pages (five at a time). If you do not have any broken links, you see a message that there are no broken links.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/ff631143e3dfa2592b0866eb4307a1796c04423d6b07b3ab84c51b33bea67c8e-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-3"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-3"></a></h3><p>Broken links are not automatically updated. You need to refresh the dashboard to update the broken links gadget.</p></blockquote>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Language</strong> – Select from the available languages to see the dashboard in that language. The content list in every tab in the workflow status displays only content of that language.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/589f344f09a4a0e0df62bd0a35ec0d5a7bef021f588a1df2ced81594753f3336-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-4"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-4"></a></h3><p>Administrators can enable the language filter options. Also, if you go to the dashboard and select Swedish (for example), you can go to another page and Swedish is maintained when you return to the dashboard. However, if you log out, the language filter is reset to the default language.</p></blockquote>
</li>
</ul>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="cms-saas-content-manager"></div><div class="heading-text">CMS (SaaS) Content Manager</div><a aria-label="Skip link to CMS (SaaS) Content Manager" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#cms-saas-content-manager"></a></h2>
<p>The CMS <strong>Content</strong> view addresses these scaling issues by displaying all content (pages, assets, and media) in a "flat" view table structure that you can filter, search, and sort to get to the content you want. See <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/manage-content-with-content-view">Manage content with Content Manager</a>.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/0b715831ce96814b4061dd5c2a3450e2166f67cff8cc877b6c4744cf678d2880-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="cms-saas-edit-view"></div><div class="heading-text">CMS (SaaS) Edit view</div><a aria-label="Skip link to CMS (SaaS) Edit view" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#cms-saas-edit-view"></a></h2>
<p>Content managers primarily use CMS (Saas) to edit their content using <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/get-started-with-visual-builder">Visual Builder</a> and the <a target="_self" href="/hc/en-us/articles/27677023087501">All Properties editing view</a>. Visual Builder is the editor interface in CMS (SaaS) that makes content creation and layout building intuitive and accessible to non-technical users.</p>
<p>Content managers can design, modify, and reuse layout templates (blueprints) directly in Visual Builder and create adaptable experiences for any channel without developer involvement. Front-end developers can also create <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/select-styles">styles</a> that you can pick to help you adhere to your brand's guidelines.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/157d2ebb37ae0a8b0946fdac0b9499ba54a32f2cf4e45f8d38802dcc1386e01f-63b018252e080e15b423b6e8875ba7e6f3d817db7c10737c0552d44b793595cd-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<p>The <strong>toolbar</strong> and the <strong>panes</strong> in the CMS (SaaS) edit view provide access to functions when working with content. When entering the edit view, you have the top menu and the toolbar at the top, and adjustable panes to the left and right.</p>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="cms-saas-reports-view"></div><div class="heading-text">CMS (SaaS) Reports view</div><a aria-label="Skip link to CMS (SaaS) Reports view" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#cms-saas-reports-view"></a></h2>
<p>Reports are valuable tools for content editors, application owners, marketers, and merchandisers to monitor various application activities. CMS (SaaS) has built-in reports.</p>
<p>When you generate a report, select the desired report and the starting point in the page tree from where you want the report to include data, then click <strong>Show Report</strong>. You can filter data by time and language, and pages included in the report results open in edit page when you click a page link.</p>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-5"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-5"></a></h3><p>Some reports rely on scheduled jobs running in the background to generate report data. See <a target="_self" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4413192306317">Scheduled jobs</a>.</p></blockquote>
<p>Select <strong>Type of Report</strong> to display a report about one of the following subjects:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Not Published Pages</strong> – Displays pages that have not been published and have a last changed date within a certain period. Select a page from the list of report results to open it. </li>
<li><strong>Published Pages</strong> – Displays pages published within a certain period. Select a page from the list of report results to open it.</li>
<li><strong>Changed Pages</strong> – Displays pages with a changed date within a certain period. Select a page from the list of report results to open it.</li>
<li><strong>Expired Pages</strong> – Displays pages with a stop publish date within a certain period. Select a page from the list of report results to open it.</li>
<li><strong>Simple Addresses</strong> – Displays published pages that have a simple address. Select a page from the list of report results to open it.</li>
<li><strong>Link Status</strong> – Displays unreachable links, perhaps due to a page being moved, an application shut down, or a momentary outage of a target link.</li>
</ul>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/db219355939989b99bc4db6d4774fe8e66644243c96a273d63cd0789b663c96a-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="cms-saas-settings-view"></div><div class="heading-text">CMS (SaaS) Settings view</div><a aria-label="Skip link to CMS (SaaS) Settings view" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#cms-saas-settings-view"></a></h2>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-6"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-6"></a></h3><p>CMS (SaaS) administrators and developers with administrator access rights manage the following CMS (SaaS) user interface <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/settings">settings</a>.</p></blockquote>
<ul>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/content-types-1">Content Types</a></li>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/applications">Applications</a></li>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/blueprints">Blueprints</a></li>
<li><strong>Access rights</strong>
<ul>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/api-keys">API Keys</a></li>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/access-rights">Set Access Rights</a></li>
</ul>
</li>

<ul>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/scheduled-jobs">Scheduled Jobs</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
<li><strong>Config</strong>

<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/edit-tabs">Edit Tabs</a></li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/export-data-from-cms-saas">Export data</a></li>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/import-data-into-cms-saas">Import data</a></li>

<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/change-log">Change Log</a></li>
<li><a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/search-configuration">Search Configuration</a></li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/89f24b8c6c51a517dbddf7b057634b99aa7c67ee25db5e219fe0479a2fbb9a05-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="my-settings"></div><div class="heading-text">My settings</div><a aria-label="Skip link to My settings" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#my-settings"></a></h2>
<p>You can change some of your personal account settings by going to the top menu > your avatar > <strong>My settings</strong>.</p>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-7"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-7"></a></h3><p>Your username is set in your identity provider (such as Opti ID) and cannot be changed in CMS.</p></blockquote>
<p>In the <strong>Display Options</strong> tab, you have the following settings:</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/1aeaffaab121e5b2c3927c48272dab1ffe3307cd4d74b36cbdc5862e89d5595a-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Personal language</strong> – You can select your desired user interface language from the drop-down list. This setting affects the language of the user interface, such as text in buttons and dialog boxes. It does not affect the language of your website.</p>
<p>CMS (SaaS) supports 12 user interface languages. English is the master language, and the others are translated languages. You can have many more <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/languages">content languages</a>.</p>
<ul>
<li>DA – Danish</li>
<li>DE – German</li>
<li>EN – English</li>
<li>ES – Spanish</li>
<li>FI – Finnish</li>
<li>FR – French</li>
<li>IT – Italian</li>
<li>JA – Japanese</li>
<li>NL – Dutch</li>
<li>NO – Norwegian</li>
<li>SV – Swedish</li>
<li>ZH – Simplified Chinese</li>
</ul>
<p>See the <a target="_self" href="#set-a-personal-language-preference">Set a personal language preference</a> section.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Views – Limit touch support</strong> – On touchscreen devices, browsers can have difficulty prioritizing between screen input and computer-mouse input. This sometimes makes it impossible to resize panes using the computer mouse. If you experience problems with CMS and the touchscreen, enable the <strong>Limit touch support</strong> feature. This feature prioritizes computer mouse input over touchscreen input and enables the computer mouse to interact with drag and drop, resizing panes, and so on.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Reset Views</strong> – You can reset your user interface views to the settings. If you have changes to the user interfaces, such as added, moved, or deleted gadgets, these changes are undone, and the default views are displayed.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="set-a-personal-language-preference"></div><div class="heading-text">Set a personal language preference</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Set a personal language preference" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#set-a-personal-language-preference"></a></h3>
<p>You can set the preferred UI language in your user profile.</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Select your user profile avatar > <strong>My Settings</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your preferred language from the <strong>Personal Language</strong> drop-down list in the <strong>Display Options</strong> tab.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/f8c9e451810542f073724c97d4c8699232694e7f539915609f279105b9d808cb-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>. The user interface displays the selected language.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/02e58637000ff05cd2f94a091e42c324d8af00ff2c74612fbd9aeb182cd8615f-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
</ol>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="gadgets"></div><div class="heading-text">Gadgets</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Gadgets" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#gadgets"></a></h2>
<p>A <strong>gadget</strong> is a small application added to the assets and navigation panes in CMS (SaaS).</p>
<p>Select <strong>Add Gadgets</strong>, and select a gadget to add from the list of available gadgets.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/736c709f22eeaa9dd9954a83f291196e4348f7892410f25536ab368f146a41df-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<p>The <strong>Gadgets</strong> dialog box displays.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-center border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/c63bef3d762ed5e80c7fc7522f88c9ba22548fb499fbe213502ca64eb7a39f8f-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Media</strong> – Used to access media files (default in the assets pane).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Recent</strong> – Displays items you have viewed during your current browser session.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Recently changed</strong> – Displays recently changed content on the application.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Shared Blocks</strong> – Used to access shared blocks (default in the assets pane).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Tasks</strong> – Displays tasks to be done on the application. This gadget lets you filter items on status. You can, for example, see a list of items set as <strong>Ready to Publish</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Versions</strong> – Lets you manage content history, track changes, and control publishing workflows to ensure content governance and collaboration. See also <a target="_self" href="/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/compare-versions-of-content">Compare versions of content</a> for information on working with versions. The <strong>Versions</strong> gadget can display the following statuses for content versions:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p>Draft</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Published</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>In review</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Previously Published</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Ready to Publish</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Rejected</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>NotCreated</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>CheckedOut</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>AwaitingApproval</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>CheckedIn</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>DelayedPublish (Scheduled to publish on)</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/983513db08a17bc7bf93a0e5e729885920bf4fabe63d3d24ac0d2df4f0ad4fb1-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-8"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-8"></a></h3><p>There is a 20-version limit in the CMS (SaaS) <strong>Versions</strong> gadget.</p></blockquote>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p>To move or remove a gadget:</p>
<ul>
<li>Select <strong>Rearrange Gadgets</strong>, select a gadget, and drag it to the desired position on the dashboard or in a panel.</li>
<li>Select <strong>Rearrange Gadgets</strong>, and click the <strong>Remove gadget</strong> symbol next to the gadget you want to remove from the dashboard or pane.</li>
</ul>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="user-interface-elements"></div><div class="heading-text">User interface elements</div><a aria-label="Skip link to User interface elements" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#user-interface-elements"></a></h2>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Product chooser</strong> – Select which Optimizely product to work with if you have more than one.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/66777db2506e694fe279d97f7e523c4cb2d68fdffa527056bfdaa16ff6c2f08c-CMS-SaaS-product-chooser.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Left navigation bar</strong> – Access to <strong>Dashboard</strong>, <strong>Edit</strong>, <strong>Reports</strong>, and <strong>Settings</strong>.<br>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/a0e57a1216b2e9e4e8e2f48ebe37f796a3a208c2933e0409c4b86e8f80f3205d-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Settings</strong> – Edit settings for the Content tree.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/a3e6f9c7c0f957127aa1620007a38af91dd2f1274f0c695fbd35c993ae7c998b-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Panel pin</strong> – Expand and lock the Content tree or Assets panels in an open position.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/e71bf108683f0985b9b7bf19473d68be232d69d4626353c4e69bc3dbaf6f0171-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Toggle navigation pane</strong> – Toggle to display or hide the Content tree.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/851df572f69a95d1d6dc9619b4565766ce87be5a535ef0b36d74397f1f36ca9d-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Create content</strong> – Create a page or shared block.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/93cf1caed166e9b4e384e9f82a9e9e7022a925bff18061bb6c6ee1636869433b-image.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Breadcrumb</strong> – See the hierarchy of the content tree and click for quick access. For example: <em>Vacations Unlimited / Beaches</em>). Click the title to rename it or open the <strong>More (...)</strong> menu for other options.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/fba7aa2e14c3c423074d386439e6591cf76d2e6fdb66c13c3d8054b541ceabdd-Saas-breadcrumbs.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Content tree</strong> – See the page tree structure (Pages) and tasks management (Tasks).</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/7000e76133cb4bc30a52d86e902d2c897557d094b96d6b081e13db7f2d4dd25f-SaaS-content-tree.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Outline pane</strong> – See a list view of your sections. You can drag and drop a section in any order or go to the content you want to edit by hovering over the section in the preview or the outline.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="" class="img img-align-left border" height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/2244b6c4ea7626a49f313d5f3b665a31349f58227aa78663014cc03ef7c80025-SaaS-outline.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>

<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="cms-users-and-related-tasks"></div><div class="heading-text">CMS users and related tasks</div><a aria-label="Skip link to CMS users and related tasks" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#cms-users-and-related-tasks"></a></h2>
<p>A <em>user</em> is someone who logs in to the CMS (SaaS) user interface to work with different parts of the platform. Users can belong to one or more user groups and have different roles, depending on which parts of the Optimizely platform they use, their tasks, and the size and set up of the organization.</p>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-10"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-10"></a></h3><p>Administrators manage users and groups through Opti ID.</p><ul>
<li>To add users, see <a target="_self" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/15858067637389-Manage-users">Manage users</a> in the Opti ID documentation.</li>
<li>To add groups, see <a target="_self" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/15858201786765-Manage-groups">Manage groups</a> in the Opti ID documentation.</li>
<li>To set roles and permissions for users and groups, see <a target="_self" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/15858154659853-Manage-roles-and-permissions">Manage roles and permissions</a> in the Opti ID documentation.</li>
</ul></blockquote>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="content-managers"></div><div class="heading-text">Content Managers</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Content Managers" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#content-managers"></a></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Content editor</strong> – A <em>content editor</em> is someone with access to the editorial interface who creates and publishes content on the application. Content editors, who understand the application content, work with search optimization for selected content in search results. Editors may also want to follow up on content with unusually high or low conversion rates to update or delete this content.</li>
<li><strong>Marketer</strong> – A <em>marketer</em> creates omnichannel campaigns and content with targeted banner advertisements to ensure customers get a consistent on-site experience. The marketer also monitors campaign KPIs to optimize page conversion. A marketer who understands the application content may also optimize search for campaigns and promote content using personalization features.</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="content-administrators"></div><div class="heading-text">Content administrators</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Content administrators" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#content-administrators"></a></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Administrator</strong> – An <em>administrator</em> configures system settings from the administration user interface, including search, languages, personalization, and user access. Administrators usually have extended access rights compared to other user groups and can access all parts of the Optimizely platform. They may also have administration access to integrated third-party systems. The administrator may also be the contact person to communicate with the application developers.</li>
<li><strong>Application owner</strong> – An <em>application owner</em> is someone with overall business or technical responsibility for the content and performance of one or more applications. The application owner may monitor reports for activities such as page conversions, customer reviews, or sales progress; rarely creates content but can be involved in the approval of content created by others. An application owner may also have administrative access and be the owner of mailing clients used for organizing campaign mailings.</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="developers"></div><div class="heading-text">Developers</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Developers" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#developers"></a></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Developer</strong> – A <em>developer</em> is someone with source code access and programming skills. Developers work with application configuration, implementation, maintenance, and functionality development. Developers may also install integrations and third-party extensions. Developers may be associated directly with the organization owning the application or with an external partner company.</li>
</ul>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="additional-roles"></div><div class="heading-text">Additional roles</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Additional roles" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#additional-roles"></a></h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Community member and moderator</strong> – A <em>community member</em> or a visitor can add content if social features and community functionality are available for the application. This content includes forum and blog postings, reviews, ratings, and comments, in which case an editor or a specific <em>moderator</em> role for large applications and online communities may need to monitor this type of content on the application.</li>
<li><strong>Recipient</strong> – A <em>recipient</em> is an individual who has opted-in to receive emails from a business, for example, when purchasing from the application. Recipients and their associated data are managed in recipient lists used for omnichannel marketing. You can track and analyze recipient actions, such as clicking links in an email and providing input to application owners and users for further marketing actions.</li>
<li><strong>Visitor</strong> – A <em>visitor</em> is someone who visits an application to find information or to use services. Visitors may also contribute to application content as community members, which usually requires registration of an account profile.</li>
</ul></div></div><div align="center" class="Flex Flex_row " justify="between" style="--flex-gap: var(--md);"><div class="UpdatedAt"><p class="DateLine "><i class="icon icon-watch"></i>Updated 2 days (function () {
  /* ===== CONFIG ===== */
  const DEBUG = /\boasdebug=1\b/i.test(location.search);
  const FALLBACK_DELAY_MS = 5000;
  const log = (...a) => DEBUG && console.log('[oas-link]', ...a);

  /* ===== GUARD ===== */
  if (window.__OAS_DL_INIT__) return;
  window.__OAS_DL_INIT__ = true;

  /* ===== STATE ===== */
  const CACHE = new Map();
  let currentAbort = null;
  let runTimer     = null;
  let lastCtxKey   = null;
  let loadSeq      = 0;
  let activeCtxKey = null;
  let activeLoadId = null;
  const fbTimers   = new Map();

  /* ===== STYLES ===== */
  function ensureStyles() {
    if (document.getElementById('oas-link-style')) return;
    const s = document.createElement('style');

  const getHead      = () => document.querySelector('#content-head');
  const getH1        = () => document.querySelector('#content-head h1');
  const getHeaderRoot = () =>
    document.querySelector('header[data-raycast-oas]') ||
    getHead()?.closest('header') ||
    document.querySelector('header');

  function getSlot() {
    ensureStyles();
    const head = getHead();
    if (!head) return null;
    let slot = head.querySelector('#oas-slot');
    if (!slot) {
      slot = document.createElement('div');
      slot.id = 'oas-slot';
      const h1 = getH1();
      if (h1) h1.insertAdjacentElement('afterend', slot);
      else head.appendChild(slot);
    }
    return slot;
  }

  function removeSlot() {
    getHead()?.querySelector('#oas-slot')?.remove();
    setHeadState(null);
  }

  function setHeadState(state) {
    getHead()?.classList.toggle('oas-loading', state === 'loading');
  }

  /* ===== RENDER ===== */
  function renderLoading(loadId) {
    const slot = getSlot();
    if (!slot) return;
    if (slot.querySelector('[data-oas-loading]')?.getAttribute('data-oas-loading') === String(loadId)) return;
    if (slot.querySelector('[data-oas-link],[data-oas-msg]')) return;
    setHeadState('loading');
    slot.innerHTML = `
      <div class="oas-inline" data-oas-loading="${loadId}" aria-live="polite">
        <span class="oas-spin" aria-hidden="true"></span>
        <span>Resolving API spec…</span>
      </div>
    `;
  }

  function renderButton(result) {
    const slot = getSlot();
    if (!slot) return;
    setHeadState('ready');
    slot.innerHTML = `
      <a class="oas-link-btn" data-oas-link="true"
         href="${result.downloadUrl || result.url}"
         download="${result.filename}" rel="noopener">Download API spec</a>
    `;
  }

  function renderFallback() {
    const slot = getSlot();
    if (!slot) return;
    setHeadState('fallback');
    slot.innerHTML = `
      <div class="oas-inline" data-oas-msg="true">
        <span>Having trouble finding the proper spec? <a href="${projectRoot()}/openapi">View all API specs</a>.</span>
      </div>
    `;
  }

  function scheduleFallback(loadId) {
    cancelFallback(loadId);
    fbTimers.set(loadId, setTimeout(() => {
      const slot = getSlot();
      const cur = slot?.querySelector('[data-oas-loading]')?.getAttribute('data-oas-loading');
      if (cur === String(loadId) && !slot.querySelector('[data-oas-link]')) renderFallback();
    }, FALLBACK_DELAY_MS));
  }
  function cancelFallback(loadId) {
    clearTimeout(fbTimers.get(loadId));
    fbTimers.delete(loadId);
  }

  /* ===== CONTEXT ===== */
  const isInReference = () => location.pathname.includes('/reference/');
  const projectRoot   = () => location.pathname.replace(/\/reference.*/, '');
  const currentSlug   = () => (location.pathname.match(/\/reference\/([^/?#]+)/)||[])[1] || null;

  function readmeVersion() {
    const v = document.querySelector('meta[name="readme-version"]')?.content || '';
    if (!v || v === 'default') return null;
    return v.startsWith('v') ? v.slice(1) : v;
  }

  function isRealEndpoint() {
    const header = getHeaderRoot();
    if (!header) return false;
    const method = header.querySelector('[data-testid="http-method"]')?.textContent?.trim().toLowerCase() || '';
    const methodOk = /^(get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options)$/.test(method);
    const hasUrl   = !!header.querySelector('[data-testid="serverurl"], [data-testid="request-url"]');
    return !!(methodOk && (hasUrl || header.hasAttribute('data-raycast-oas')));
  }

  /* ===== NETWORK ===== */
  async function headOk(url, signal) {
    try { const r = await fetch(url, { method: 'HEAD', credentials: 'include', signal }); return r.ok; }
    catch { return false; }
  }
  const absoluteUrl = (u) => { try { return new URL(u, location.origin).href; } catch { return null; } };

  /* ===== FALLBACK: name-match against /openapi index ===== */
  // Used only when data-raycast-oas is absent. Scores each listed spec by how
  // many tokens from the project root path appear in its filename, then picks
  // the best match without fetching any spec content.
  async function findFromOpenapiIndex(signal) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`${projectRoot()}/openapi`, { credentials: 'include', signal });
      if (!res.ok) return null;
      const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(await res.text(), 'text/html');
      const links = [...doc.querySelectorAll('a[href$=".json"]')].map(a => a.getAttribute('href')).filter(Boolean);
      const tokens = projectRoot().replace(/^\//, '').split(/[-/]+/).filter(t => t.length > 3);
      const best = links
        .map(href => ({ href, score: tokens.reduce((s, t) => s + (href.toLowerCase().includes(t) ? 1 : 0), 0) }))
        .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)[0];
      if (!best || best.score === 0) return null;
      const filename = best.href.split('/').pop();
      const url = absoluteUrl(`${projectRoot()}/openapi/${filename}`);
      return url ? { url, downloadUrl: url, filename } : null;

  async function waitForHead(timeoutMs = 3000) {
    if (getHead()) return true;
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      const obs = new MutationObserver(() => { if (getHead()) { obs.disconnect(); resolve(true); } });
      obs.observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      setTimeout(() => { obs.disconnect(); resolve(!!getHead()); }, timeoutMs);
    });
  }

  async function run() {
    if (!isInReference()) { moHead.disconnect(); moSide.disconnect(); moHdr.disconnect(); return; }

    if (!getHead()) {
      if (!(await waitForHead(3000))) { scheduleRun('no-head-yet'); return; }
      if (!getHead()) { scheduleRun('no-head-postwait'); return; }
    }

    bindObservers();

    if (!isRealEndpoint()) { removeSlot(); scheduleRun('await-endpoint-hydration'); return; }

    const start = performance.now();
    while (!getH1() && performance.now() - start < 800) await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(r));

    const ver        = readmeVersion() || 'default';
    const slug       = currentSlug() || '';
    const raycastKey = getHeaderRoot()?.getAttribute('data-raycast-oas') || '';
    const ctxKey     = `${ver}::${slug}::${raycastKey}`;
    const slot       = getSlot();

    if (activeCtxKey === ctxKey && currentAbort && !currentAbort.signal.aborted) { log('dedupe: in-flight'); return; }
    if (ctxKey === lastCtxKey && slot?.querySelector('[data-oas-link],[data-oas-msg]')) { log('skip: already rendered'); return; }
    lastCtxKey = ctxKey;

    if (CACHE.has(ctxKey)) { renderButton(CACHE.get(ctxKey)); return; }

    const myLoadId = ++loadSeq;
    activeCtxKey = ctxKey;
    activeLoadId = myLoadId;
    renderLoading(myLoadId);
    scheduleFallback(myLoadId);
    if (currentAbort) currentAbort.abort();
    currentAbort = new AbortController();
    const { signal } = currentAbort;

    try {
      // Primary: <header data-raycast-oas="..."> is ReadMe's authoritative signal
      // for exactly which spec this page was built from.
      if (raycastKey) {
        const filename   = raycastKey.split('/').pop();
        const openapiUrl = `${projectRoot()}/openapi/${filename}`;
        const url = (await headOk(openapiUrl, signal)) ? openapiUrl : absoluteUrl(raycastKey);
        if (myLoadId !== activeLoadId) return;
        if (url) { const r = { url, downloadUrl: url, filename }; cancelFallback(myLoadId); CACHE.set(ctxKey, r); renderButton(r); }
        return;
      }

      // Fallback: data-raycast-oas absent — name-match against /openapi index.
      const result = await findFromOpenapiIndex(signal);
      if (myLoadId !== activeLoadId) return;
      if (result) { cancelFallback(myLoadId); CACHE.set(ctxKey, result); renderButton(result); }
    } catch (e) {
      log('run error:', e);
    } finally {
      if (activeLoadId === myLoadId) { activeCtxKey = null; activeLoadId = null; }
    }
  }

  /* ===== LIFECYCLE ===== */
  function scheduleRun(why) {
    log('scheduleRun:', why);
    clearTimeout(runTimer);
    runTimer = setTimeout(run, 120);
  }

  const moHead = new MutationObserver((ms) => { if (ms.every(m => !m.target?.closest?.('#oas-slot'))) scheduleRun('mut:head'); });
  const moSide = new MutationObserver(() => scheduleRun('mut:sidebar'));
  const moHdr  = new MutationObserver((ms) => { if (ms.every(m => !m.target?.closest?.('#oas-slot'))) scheduleRun('mut:header'); });

  function bindObservers() {
    moHead.disconnect(); moSide.disconnect(); moHdr.disconnect();
    const head = getHead();
    if (head) moHead.observe(head, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    const side = document.querySelector('#reference-sidebar');
    if (side) moSide.observe(side, { childList: true, subtree: true });
    const hdr = getHeaderRoot();
    // attributes:true catches SPA updates to data-raycast-oas (attribute mutation, not childList)
    if (hdr) moHdr.observe(hdr, { childList: true, subtree: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['data-raycast-oas'] });
  }

  const onPageLoad = () => scheduleRun('pageLoad');
  if (window.jQuery && jQuery(window).on) jQuery(window).on('pageLoad', onPageLoad);
  window.addEventListener('pageLoad', onPageLoad);
  if (document.readyState === 'complete' || document.readyState === 'interactive') onPageLoad();
  else document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', onPageLoad);
  bindObservers();

Get started with CMS (SaaS)                                                           

For AI agents: visit https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/llms.txt for an index of all pages formatted in Markdown and endpoints in OpenAPI.

Optimizely Content Management System (CMS) (SaaS) provides web content management through a UI that lets users work efficiently with content.

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> [](#note)
> 
> Before editors can create content in CMS (SaaS), administrators and developers must implement a [content model](/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/content-modeling-saas) that is modular and reusable to ensure consistency and reduce redundancy. A robust content model supports your project's immediate needs and its long-term evolution.
> 
> See [an interactive demo](https://optimizely.navattic.com/cms-content-modeling) on how to approach content modeling in Optimizely CMS (SaaS) and Visual Builder.

Enter your username and password in the Optimizely login dialog box, and click **Log In**.

After logging in, your implementation and [access rights](/content-management-system/v1.0.0-CMS-SaaS/docs/access-rights) control the options you see.

## 

General features

[](#general-features)

*   **Context-sensitive actions** – Some features are only available in certain contexts. The toolbar (for example) presents relevant actions depending on what you are currently doing, and the add (+) button also offers context-sensitive options.
*   **Primary actions** – Some actions open in a window, such as a page delete confirmation. The background is then dimmed, meaning you must finish the primary action to continue.
*   **Action feedback and notifications** – A message in the notification bar confirms successful actions. A notification may also display if an error requires you to take action.
*   **Drag-and-drop operations** – Drag-and-drop is supported in many areas. For example, you can drag pages, media files, and shared blocks into the rich-text area or content areas or rearrange the page tree structure using drag-and-drop.
*   **Tooltips** – Hover over a button or field, and a short tooltip displays.
*   **Keyboard commands** – Standard keyboard commands are supported in many areas, such as moving pages in the page tree or the rich-text editor.
*   **Search** – Supported in many areas to locate, such as pages in the page tree or media in the folder structure.
*   **Adaptable work environment** – Resize and pin the panes depending on what you are currently doing, and add and remove gadgets of your choice for quick access to functionality.
*   **Support for time zones** – Publishing actions in the edit view is done in your local time zone, whereas administrative actions are based on server time.
*   **Context menus** – Available in many areas, such as the panes, page tree, and item listings. The menu displays different options depending on where you are in the interface and what you are doing.

### 

Content Managers

[](#content-managers)

*   **Content editor** – A _content editor_ is someone with access to the editorial interface who creates and publishes content on the application. Content editors, who understand the application content, work with search optimization for selected content in search results. Editors may also want to follow up on content with unusually high or low conversion rates to update or delete this content.
*   **Marketer** – A _marketer_ creates omnichannel campaigns and content with targeted banner advertisements to ensure customers get a consistent on-site experience. The marketer also monitors campaign KPIs to optimize page conversion. A marketer who understands the application content may also optimize search for campaigns and promote content using personalization features.

### 

Content administrators

[](#content-administrators)

*   **Administrator** – An _administrator_ configures system settings from the administration user interface, including search, languages, personalization, and user access. Administrators usually have extended access rights compared to other user groups and can access all parts of the Optimizely platform. They may also have administration access to integrated third-party systems. The administrator may also be the contact person to communicate with the application developers.
*   **Application owner** – An _application owner_ is someone with overall business or technical responsibility for the content and performance of one or more applications. The application owner may monitor reports for activities such as page conversions, customer reviews, or sales progress; rarely creates content but can be involved in the approval of content created by others. An application owner may also have administrative access and be the owner of mailing clients used for organizing campaign mailings.

### 

Developers

[](#developers)

*   **Developer** – A _developer_ is someone with source code access and programming skills. Developers work with application configuration, implementation, maintenance, and functionality development. Developers may also install integrations and third-party extensions. Developers may be associated directly with the organization owning the application or with an external partner company.

### 

Additional roles

[](#additional-roles)

*   **Community member and moderator** – A _community member_ or a visitor can add content if social features and community functionality are available for the application. This content includes forum and blog postings, reviews, ratings, and comments, in which case an editor or a specific _moderator_ role for large applications and online communities may need to monitor this type of content on the application.
*   **Recipient** – A _recipient_ is an individual who has opted-in to receive emails from a business, for example, when purchasing from the application. Recipients and their associated data are managed in recipient lists used for omnichannel marketing. You can track and analyze recipient actions, such as clicking links in an email and providing input to application owners and users for further marketing actions.
*   **Visitor** – A _visitor_ is someone who visits an application to find information or to use services. Visitors may also contribute to application content as community members, which usually requires registration of an account profile.
